rule: top-level `file.fun` (file basename); nested modules/functors dotted (`file.Make.connect`); local function lets `outer.f`, local value lets fold into the enclosing binding; module-level code's caller is the module. Names resolve in definition order through local bindings, local opens, enclosing structures and their opens/includes, module aliases (`module F = Filegen.Make (P)`) and dune library wrappers (`Functoria.DSL`); then Stdlib (`Stdlib.invalid_arg`), the innermost external local open, the one external open (medium); `List.length` medium; applying a parameter is unknown.
source: KNOWN_GAP: modules written as = functor () -> struct drop their name from callers
notes: `module Make = functor (X : ...) -> struct ... end` and the generative `module Fresh = functor () -> struct ... end` are functors exactly like `module Make (X : ...) = struct`: their members are dotted under the functor name (`counter.Make.show`, `counter.Fresh.bump`), and that name appears in the caller IDs of their bodies. `module M = Make (...)` / `module F = Fresh ()` are module aliases (OCaml note), so `M.show` and `F.bump` resolve to the functor members, high. Functor applications are module bindings, not calls. `X.start` is a value reference.
